newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Veba could join Venezuela's Lagoven-Mobil venture.
newsitem.headline: Veba could join Venezuela's Lagoven-Mobil venture.

text.p: Talks between Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) subsidiary Lagoven, Mobil Corp and Veba Oil on incorporating the German company in an extra- heavy crude joint venture are nearing an agreement, Lagoven president Julius Trinkunas said.
"We're pretty near to an agreement in our conversations with Veba," Trinkunas told reporters at an international oil conference in Caracas.
Lagoven and Mobil signed a $2.3 billion deal two months ago to upgrade and sell about 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of heavy crude from the Cerro Negro area of Venezuela's Orinoco Tar Belt.
Would Veba Oil join the venture, output could be boosted to 120,000 bpd, Trinkunas said. The German firm, a unit of Germany's fourth biggest company Veba AG, would get these extra 20,000 bpd.
The Lagoven official gave no details on the financial aspects of the possible deal with Veba but said "it could be a matter of one month to reach an agreement."
Frank Alcock, manager of Mobil Venezuela, was more cautious and said "chances of reaching a deal with Veba are 50-50."
The Lagoven-Mobil project, to create a 35 year joint venture, will be presented to Venezuelan Congress before the end of the year for final approval. Production is due to start in 1999.
